headings.title: Introduction to Body Cavities
headings.content: Body cavities are internal spaces within the human body that protect, separate, and support internal organs. They are broadly divided into two main groups based on their embryonic development and location: the dorsal cavity located near the posterior surface, and the ventral cavity located near the anterior surface. These fluid-filled spaces prevent friction between moving organs, such as the beating heart or expanding lungs, and cushion them against physical trauma from the external environment.

headings.title: Dorsal Body Cavity: Cranial and Spinal Regions
headings.content:
The dorsal body cavity is situated along the posterior aspect of the body and is completely encased in bone for maximum protection of the central nervous system. It is subdivided into two continuous parts:
- **Cranial cavity**: Formed by the skull bones, this space encloses, protects, and supports the brain.
- **Spinal (vertebral) cavity**: Formed by the vertebrae of the spinal column, this long channel runs down from the brainstem to enclose the spinal cord.

headings.title: Ventral Body Cavity and the Thoracic Subdivision
headings.content: The ventral body cavity is the larger anterior cavity of the human body. It houses visceral organs collectively known as the viscera. A major muscular partition called the diaphragm separates the ventral cavity into an upper thoracic cavity and a lower abdominopelvic cavity. The thoracic cavity itself is further enclosed by the rib cage and contains the heart, lungs, major blood vessels, and the thymus gland. Within the thoracic space, smaller compartments exist: the pleural cavities surrounding each lung, and the pericardial cavity enclosing the heart.

headings.title: Abdominopelvic Cavity Organization
headings.content:
The abdominopelvic cavity is a vast continuous space situated below the diaphragm. Although it lacks a physical internal wall separating its two parts, clinicians divide it conceptually into the upper abdominal cavity and the lower pelvic cavity.
- **Abdominal cavity**: Contains digestive organs such as the stomach, intestines, liver, spleen, pancreas, and kidneys.
- **Pelvic cavity**: Contains the urinary bladder, reproductive organs, and the final segments of the large intestine.

headings.title: Abdominal Regions and Quadrants
headings.content:
To accurately document pain, physical findings, and organ locations, healthcare providers map the abdominopelvic cavity using two different systems.

| System | Division Count | Primary Use |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Quadrants | 4 areas | Quick clinical assessment and charting |
| Regions | 9 areas | Precise anatomical localization |

The four quadrants are created by drawing an imaginary horizontal and vertical line intersecting at the umbilicus, yielding the Right Upper Quadrant (RUQ), Left Upper Quadrant (LUQ), Right Lower Quadrant (RLQ), and Left Lower Quadrant (LLQ).

headings.title: Serous Membranes and Their Layers
headings.content:
Ventral body cavities contain delicate organs that move constantly. To protect them, a thin, slippery double-layered membrane called the serous membrane lines the walls and organs. 
- **Parietal layer**: The outer membrane that attaches directly to the cavity wall.
- **Visceral layer**: The inner membrane that folds inward to cover the surface of the internal organs.
Between these two layers lies a narrow potential space filled with serous fluid, which acts as a lubricant to reduce friction during organ movement like breathing or digestion.

headings.title: Clinical Significance in Nursing Assessment
headings.content: Understanding body cavities directly guides daily nursing assessments and physical examinations. When auscultating lung sounds, palpating tender abdominal areas, or inspecting surgical incisions, nurses rely on anatomical boundaries to describe findings accurately in patient records. Recognizing which organs share a specific cavity helps anticipate referred pain patterns and potential complications when trauma or infection affects one structure within that enclosed space.
